chunks: And it is narrated from Abū Ayyūb, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man performed eight circuits around the House for the obligatory tawaf. He said: “Then let him add six to it, then perform four rakʿahs.”
And in another report: “Indeed, the obligation is the second tawaf, and the first two rakʿahs are for the obligatory tawaf, while the other two rakʿahs and the first tawaf are voluntary.”

key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: around the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he performs eight circuits in the obligatory tawaf?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling for one who mistakenly performs eight circuits in the obligatory tawaf. Instead of invalidating the act entirely, he adds six more circuits, making the second set the obligatory tawaf, while the first set and an additional two rakʿahs are treated as supererogatory.
